fatal_errors: The proposed nickel-based superalloy does not reconstruct the target ZrB2 cermet containing 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder.
It omits spark plasma sintering and the critical 1500 °C processing optimum.

The cited evidence concerns general high-temperature strength, oxidation of refractory high-entropy alloys, or additive manufacturing; none demonstrates resistance of nickel-based superalloys to long-term immersion in molten aluminum.
A protective oxide layer under gaseous oxidation conditions cannot be assumed to remain protective during immersion in molten aluminum.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general need to reduce corrosion and extend equipment life in high-temperature molten aluminum, but otherwise diverges from the target. It supplies neither the ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr composition nor the densification-controlled mechanism in which the HEA binder fills pores at 1500 °C and suppresses aluminum penetration, while binder loss at 1600 °C worsens performance. Specific exposure and wear conditions, quantitative outcomes, and meaningful processing baselines are absent. The proposed comparison is broadly falsifiable through corrosion-rate and service-life measurements, but its undefined current-material baseline and unspecified temperature, duration, and testing protocol limit discrimination. Most importantly, the references do not validate nickel-superalloy compatibility with molten aluminum or the asserted protective-layer mechanism, so the proposed material remains unsupported rather than a well-evidenced alternative.
